tests.name: A-Level Biology Mock Exam
tests.description: Timed mock assembled from worked examples across the course

questions.question: [Biochemistry and Respiration] Calculate total ATP from one glucose via aerobic respiration. Explain why yield is often less than theoretical
questions.correctAnswer: Glycolysis: 2 ATP + 2 NADH (3-5 ATP); Link: 2 NADH (5 ATP); Krebs: 2 ATP + 6 NADH (15 ATP) + 2 FADH₂ (3 ATP) = 25-30 + 4 = 29-32 ATP. Less because: proton leak, shuttle costs (glycerol-3-P shuttle vs malate-aspartate), ATP for transport
questions.explanation: Glycolysis: 2 ATP + 2 NADH (3-5 ATP); Link: 2 NADH (5 ATP); Krebs: 2 ATP + 6 NADH (15 ATP) + 2 FADH₂ (3 ATP) = 25-30 + 4 = 29-32 ATP. Less because: proton leak, shuttle costs (glycerol-3-P shuttle vs malate-aspartate), ATP for transport

questions.question: [Cell Structure and Function] Explain how the structure of the mitochondria enables efficient aerobic respiration
questions.correctAnswer: Double membrane: outer permeable, inner folded into cristae (large SA for ETC). Matrix contains Krebs cycle enzymes. Intermembrane space accumulates H⁺ for chemiosmosis. Own DNA/ribosomes for some ETC proteins
questions.explanation: Double membrane: outer permeable, inner folded into cristae (large SA for ETC). Matrix contains Krebs cycle enzymes. Intermembrane space accumulates H⁺ for chemiosmosis. Own DNA/ribosomes for some ETC proteins

questions.question: [Ecology and Ecosystems] Explain why only ~10% of energy transfers between trophic levels
questions.correctAnswer: Energy lost as: heat (respiration), faeces (undigested), urine (excretion), uneaten parts. Only energy in consumed biomass available to next level. 2nd law of thermodynamics: entropy increases
questions.explanation: Energy lost as: heat (respiration), faeces (undigested), urine (excretion), uneaten parts. Only energy in consumed biomass available to next level. 2nd law of thermodynamics: entropy increases

questions.question: [Genetics and Inheritance] In sweet peas, flower colour is controlled by two genes (C and P). Both dominant alleles needed for purple flowers. Cross CcPp x CcPp. Find phenotypic ratio
questions.correctAnswer: Both genes needed for purple. C_P_ = purple (9/16); ccP_ = white (3/16); C_pp = white (3/16); ccpp = white (1/16). Ratio = 9 purple : 7 white (complementary epistasis)
questions.explanation: Both genes needed for purple. C_P_ = purple (9/16); ccP_ = white (3/16); C_pp = white (3/16); ccpp = white (1/16). Ratio = 9 purple : 7 white (complementary epistasis)

questions.question: [Homeostasis and the Nervous System] Describe how the loop of Henle creates a water potential gradient in the kidney medulla
questions.correctAnswer: Descending limb: permeable to water, impermeable to ions -> water leaves by osmosis. Ascending limb: impermeable to water, active Na⁺/Cl⁻ transport out -> filtrate diluted, medulla concentrated. Counter-current multiplier: flow in opposite directions maintains gradient
